Yes, that boundary is right for me. I saved the plain MDN link, then saved the same one with the `?utm_source=newsletter` tracking bit and the `#examples` jump-to-section tag on the end — and it recognized it as the one I already had rather than making a second copy. The count stayed at one and it just pointed me back to the existing bookmark. That's exactly what I'd want, because to me those two are the same page; the tracking junk and the "scroll to this part" marker aren't a different article.

And your reasoning matches how I think about it:

- Stripping off those tracking add-ons and the on-page section marker before deciding it's a duplicate is smart — those get tacked on all the time and shouldn't fool it into thinking it's something new.
- Being careful to leave other parts of the address alone is the right instinct too. Sometimes the bit after the address is genuinely what picks a different page — like a different item or a different entry — and in that case I'd want it treated as its own separate bookmark, not silently merged. So I'm glad you're only ignoring the parts that are known to be noise, not everything.

So this duplicate boundary is good.
